From: Prof. Anika Bose <anika.bose@midwest.edu>

Cc: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@midwest.edu>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 10:14:00 -0500
Subject: Request: matching cloud credits for summer robotics fellowship

Hi Jonas,

I hope you're well — I'm Anika Bose from the Robotics Department at Midwest Institute of Technology. We're running a 10-week summer fellowship this year where each student will fine-tune medium-sized vision+control models and run closed-loop sim experiments. Our grant funds are limited; we typically buy spot credits but the volume this summer would put us over budget.

We saw Redwood's pilot credit programs and wondered whether Redwood would consider a matching credits arrangement: Midwest would commit to a small paid reservation (we can discuss a nominal committed spend) and request up to $12,000 in promotional credits to support compute for the fellowship cohort (approx 40k tokens/day equivalent across GPUs).

Attached is a short project summary and proposed SOW that explains workloads and expected token/compute profile. Key asks:
- Eligibility confirmation for academic discount/credits
- Any documentation we should provide for institutional approval (PO/justification)
- Timeline to provision credits if approved (we start July 6)

Thanks for considering — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
Anika Bose
Professor, Robotics Dept
Midwest Institute of Technology
(attachment: Midwest-Robotics-Proposal-2026.pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: matching cloud credits for summer robotics fellowship

Hi Anika — thanks for the note and the proposal; congrats on the fellowship. I'm Jonas on the education partnerships team. Short answers up front: yes, we frequently do matching promotional credits for academic fellowships; we just need a short institutional SOW + brief usage estimate and an internal approval from our growth promotions team.

Can you confirm:
- Expected duration (you listed July start — exact end date?)
- Rough per-week GPU hours or peak concurrent GPUs (helps scoping)
- Whether any student data is sensitive (PII/PHI) — if so we'll route to security for a short review.

If you can drop the SOW into a shared Drive link (or attach here) I'll start internal approval. I can also propose a matching amount after I review usage; worst case we can do a phased provision (initial credits now, top-up after week 4).

Happy to schedule a 20-min call this week — availability Tue/Wed after 1pm CT.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Education Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and I've attached the SOW as well.
- Duration: July 6 – September 10 (10 weeks, with a final demo week)
- Peak concurrent GPUs: expect up to 8 concurrent V100-equivalent jobs during sim bursts; average concurrency ~3.
- Data sensitivity: student-submitted logs contain no PHI; we will anonymize student IDs.

Attached: Midwest-Robotics-Proposal-2026.pdf and SOW_Robotics_Pilot.xlsx

If you can propose a phased provisioning plan that would be ideal — we really need an initial allotment by July 1 to onboard the students.

Warmly,
Anika
